well: adverb
in a good, skilful or successful way
typical: verb + well: speak/play/sleep/do well. NOT for: describing a noun (use good).
She speaks English very well.
The plan worked well.
adverb
thoroughly or completely
typical: mix/shake/read well, well aware, well known. NOT for: skill.
Mix the flour and butter well.
I'm well aware of the problem.
adverb
also or in addition (as well, as well as)
typical: as well, as well as + noun. NOT for: skill.
Can I come as well?
She speaks French as well as German.
adjective
healthy
typical: feel/look/be well, get well soon. NOT for: before a noun.
I don't feel well today.
Are you well?
interjection
spoken: used to pause, think or start a new part of a conversation
typical: Well, ... at the start of a sentence. NOT for: formal writing.
Well, let's begin.
Well, I'm not sure about that.
interjection
spoken: used to express doubt, surprise or to accept a situation
typical: Well, ... / Oh well. NOT for: formal writing.
Well, I didn't think I'd see you here.
Oh well, it can't be helped.
adverb
(may/might as well) no reason not to do something
typical: might as well + verb. NOT for: health.
We might as well go home.
You may as well wait here.
work: verb
have a job and do it for pay
typical: work at/for/in + place/company. NOT for: machines.
She works at a bank.
He works for a small software company.
verb
spend time and effort doing an activity or task
typical: work in the garden/on a project. NOT for: paid jobs only.
I'm working on my essay.
He worked in the garden all afternoon.
verb
try hard over time to achieve something
typical: work hard/towards/to + verb. NOT for: machines.
They are working to improve the service.
She worked hard to pass her exams.
verb
(of a machine or equipment) operate correctly
typical: thing + work, doesn't work. NOT for: people's jobs.
The printer doesn't work.
Does the lift work today?
verb
be effective or successful
typical: a plan/method/medicine works. NOT for: machines starting.
The plan worked perfectly.
This medicine works quickly.
noun
a job or paid employment
typical: go to work, be out of work, look for work. NOT for: effort in general.
I go to work by bus.
He has been out of work for a year.
noun
effort or tasks that need to be done
typical: a lot of work, hard work, homework. NOT for: employment.
I have a lot of work today.
It took a lot of hard work.
